summary: Connect rendered assemblies to independent rigid bodies and colliders with one authoritative simulation state.
objective: Toggle collider visualization: rendered surfaces and collision boundaries agree at the contact region.
example_prompts: Connect rendered assemblies to independent rigid bodies and colliders with one authoritative simulation state.

principles: Three.js draws the view; the physics world owns dynamic poses. Give each body an explicit corresponding presentation root.
Use a solver only when the interaction requires it; an analytic trajectory can remain a smaller, clearly scoped model.
implementation: Choose consistent distance units and axes, record the installed Three.js/Rapier versions and await engine initialization before starting controls.
Create bodies and colliders separately. Configure density or mass, friction and restitution deliberately; optical materials do not supply these values.
Step the physics world at a declared fixed interval, then copy body position and quaternion into unscaled view roots. Interpolate only the rendered pose.
Use forces or impulses for dynamic actions. For prescribed motion use the appropriate kinematic target API; clear the accumulator on reset.

Build body and collider as two descriptors: `const body = world.createRigidBody( RAPIER.RigidBodyDesc.dynamic() );` then `world.createCollider( RAPIER.ColliderDesc.cuboid( hx, hy, hz ), body );` where the cuboid arguments are half-extents in the scene's declared distance unit, not full dimensions.

Set inertial properties on the collider deliberately: `.setDensity( d )` has a documented default of `1.0` and a non-zero density adds the collider's mass and angular inertia to the body it is attached to; `.setMass( m )` and `.setMassProperties( ... )` are the explicit alternatives. Choose one and record it, rather than leaving the default and compensating with a force.

Contact response is two named coefficients: `.setFriction( f )`, documented default `0.5`, and `.setRestitution( r )`, each with an optional combine rule such as `.setFrictionCombineRule( RAPIER.CoefficientCombineRule.Min )` or `.setRestitutionCombineRule( ... )`. A material's optical `roughness` supplies neither value and must not be reused as one.
observable_checks: Toggle collider visualization: rendered surfaces and collision boundaries agree at the contact region.
Apply one impulse, pause and reset; the view follows body state and never fights a second animation writer.

known_limits: Kinematic targets are not obstacle avoidance. Verify engine-specific collision filters, sensor flags and initialization in the installed version.
Authored reusable guidance; no runtime artifact or improvement has been observed for this record.
creative_affordances: Adapt proportions, finish and presentation to the scene; explain deliberate departures from this guidance.

claims.statement: Rapier colliders define mass properties and friction/restitution parameters for contact.
claims.scope: Physics configuration, separate from rendering materials.
